en.26:57: Those who had arrested Jesus led Him away to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
en.26:58: But Peter followed Him at a distance, right up to the courtyard of the high priest. And he went in and sat down with the guards to see the outcome.
en.26:59: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking false testimony against Jesus in order to put Him to death.
en.26:60: But they did not find any, though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward
en.26:61: and declared, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”
en.26:62: So the high priest stood up and asked Him, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”
en.26:63: But Jesus remained silent. Then the high priest said to Him, “I charge You under oath by the living God: Tell us if You are the Christ, the Son of God.”
en.26:64: “You have said it yourself,” Jesus answered. “But I say to all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
en.26:65: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “He has blasphemed! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.
en.26:66: What do you think?” “He deserves to die,” they answered.
en.26:67: Then they spit in His face and struck Him. Others slapped Him
en.26:68: and said, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit You?”

en.14:53: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled.
en.14:54: Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he sat with the officers and warmed himself by the fire.
en.14:55: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they did not find any.
en.14:56: For many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent.
en.14:57: Then some men stood up and testified falsely against Him:
en.14:58: “We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’”
en.14:59: But even their testimony was inconsistent.
en.14:60: So the high priest stood up before them and questioned Jesus, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”
en.14:61: But Jesus remained silent and made no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
en.14:62: “I am,” said Jesus, “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
en.14:63: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “Why do we need any more witnesses?
en.14:64: You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?” And they all condemned Him as deserving of death.
en.14:65: Then some of them began to spit on Him. They blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, and said to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers received Him with slaps in His face.

en.22:63: The men who were holding Jesus began to mock Him and beat Him.
en.22:64: They blindfolded Him and kept demanding, “Prophesy! Who hit You?”
en.22:65: And they said many other blasphemous things against Him.
en.22:66: At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and scribes, met together. They led Jesus into their Sanhedrin and said,
en.22:67: “If You are the Christ, tell us.” Jesus answered, “If I tell you, you will not believe.
en.22:68: And if I ask you a question, you will not answer.
en.22:69: But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
en.22:70: So they all asked, “Are You then the Son of God?” He replied, “You say that I am.”
en.22:71: “Why do we need any more testimony?” they declared. “We have heard it for ourselves from His own lips.”

en.18:13: They brought Him first to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
en.18:14: Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it would be better if one man died for the people.
en.18:19: Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and His teaching.
en.18:20: “I have spoken openly to the world,” Jesus answered. “I always taught in the synagogues and at the temple, where all the Jews come together. I said nothing in secret.
en.18:21: Why are you asking Me? Ask those who heard My message. Surely they know what I said.”
en.18:22: When Jesus had said this, one of the officers standing nearby slapped Him in the face and said, “Is this how You answer the high priest?”
en.18:23: Jesus replied, “If I said something wrong, testify as to what was wrong. But if I spoke correctly, why did you strike Me?”
en.18:24: Then Annas sent Him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
